context: Operations meeting of a small online shop. Sam leads operations. Current plan: two support agents, support hours 9 to 17, website redesign starts in May, the database stays on the current provider. Monthly support budget is $6,000.

lines.text: Thanks both for joining. Today we settle three things, staffing, redesign and the database.

lines.speaker: Vera
lines.text: We are drowning in tickets after the holiday sale, and two agents cannot cope.
Understood. Give me your recommendation on staffing.

lines.speaker: Vera
lines.text: I am hiring two contractors for the next three months to clear the backlog.
That affects the support budget, I will check the numbers.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: The redesign will wait until September, because the checkout fixes take all my time.
Then the plan moves by four months.

lines.speaker: Vera
lines.text: From next week support hours run from eight to eighteen, so we cover both ends of the day.
I will update the hours on the site.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: We keep the database with the current provider and we revisit it in January.
Good, one less thing to move now.

lines.speaker: Vera
lines.text: I will send the contractor job posts to the team by Wednesday.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Weekend cover stays with the on-call rota, we are not changing that.
Fine, that matches the current setup.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: My neighbour started drilling at seven this morning.
That is a rough start to the day.

lines.speaker: Vera
lines.text: I am on my second coffee already.
